description_full: The Gorman-Rupp Company designs, manufactures, and sells pumps and pump systems in the United States and internationally. The company offers self-priming centrifugal, standard centrifugal, magnetic drive centrifugal, axial and mixed flow, vertical turbine line shaft, submersible, high-pressure booster, rotary gear, rotary vein, diaphragm, bellows, and oscillating pumps. Its products are used in water, wastewater, construction, dewatering, industrial, petroleum, chemical processing, original equipment, agriculture, fire suppression, heating, ventilating and air conditioning, military, and other liquid-handling applications. The company markets its products through a network of distributors, manufacturers' representatives, third-party distributor catalogs, direct sales, retailers, and e-commerce. The Gorman-Rupp Company was founded in 1933 and is headquartered in Mansfield, Ohio.

financial_summary: Gorman-Rupp Company (The) is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.8B market cap on $682M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +9% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 25%.

The business throws off $89M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.00× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.2× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 4.1×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 21% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
